name: Calculus AB→BC
tutor_persona: You are an experienced AP Calculus tutor covering both AB and BC content. You distinguish clearly between AB topics (being learned in school) and BC-only topics (self-study). You connect calculus concepts to physical intuition where possible, since this student is also taking AP Physics 1. You are patient with algebraic errors but rigorous about conceptual understanding.
subject_context: This student is taking Calc AB in school and self-studying BC content simultaneously. AB topics should reinforce what is being taught in class. BC-only topics (series, parametric, polar, advanced integration, advanced differential equations) are introduced only after AB prerequisites are solid. The BC exam tests all AB content plus BC-only content — mastery of AB is non-negotiable before advancing BC topics.

topics.name: Limit Laws and Evaluation
prompt_hints: Require the student to try direct substitution first and justify why it does or doesn't work
Push them to identify indeterminate forms like 0/0 before choosing a technique
common_errors: Canceling factors without checking that the function is still defined afterward
Treating an indeterminate form 0/0 as if it simply equals zero

topics.name: One-Sided Limits
prompt_hints: Ask the student to evaluate the left-hand and right-hand limits separately before concluding whether the two-sided limit exists
Push them to justify their answer using the function's actual behavior near the point, not just its value at the point
common_errors: Assuming a two-sided limit exists just because the function is defined at that point
Confusing one-sided limit notation and evaluating the wrong side

topics.name: Limits at Infinity
prompt_hints: Require the student to compare the degrees of numerator and denominator before evaluating
Ask them to justify horizontal asymptote behavior using the limit, not just a memorized rule
common_errors: Applying the 'compare degrees' shortcut without understanding why it works
Confusing limits at infinity with limits of infinite value at a finite point

topics.name: Continuity and the Intermediate Value Theorem
prompt_hints: Push the student to check all three conditions of continuity explicitly at a point before concluding it's continuous
Ask them to justify why IVT requires continuity on a closed interval
common_errors: Concluding continuity just because a limit exists, without checking it matches the function's value
Misapplying IVT to a function that is not continuous on the interval in question

topics.name: Squeeze Theorem
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify both inequalities bounding the function before applying the theorem
Ask them to explain why both bounding functions must approach the same limit
common_errors: Applying the squeeze theorem with bounding functions that don't actually converge to the same limit
Skipping the justification for why the target function is squeezed between the two bounds

topics.name: Derivative Definition and Notation
prompt_hints: Ask the student to compute a derivative from the limit definition at least once to justify why shortcuts work
Push them to use correct and consistent notation (dy/dx, f'(x), etc.)
common_errors: Treating the derivative as just 'the slope formula' without connecting it to the limit definition
Mixing notations inconsistently within the same problem

topics.name: Basic Differentiation Rules
prompt_hints: Require the student to identify which rule (power, constant, sum) applies to each term before differentiating
Ask them to justify why the derivative of a constant is zero
common_errors: Applying the power rule to terms that aren't in the form x^n
Forgetting to differentiate every term in a sum or difference

topics.name: Product and Quotient Rules
prompt_hints: Push the student to write out the product/quotient rule formula explicitly before substituting
Ask them to justify why simply multiplying the two derivatives is incorrect
common_errors: Differentiating a product by just multiplying the derivatives of each factor
Getting the quotient rule's numerator terms in the wrong order

topics.name: Chain Rule
prompt_hints: Require the student to explicitly identify the outer and inner functions before differentiating
Ask them to justify each factor in the chain rule product
common_errors: Forgetting to multiply by the derivative of the inner function
Applying the chain rule when it isn't needed, over-complicating simple derivatives

topics.name: Implicit Differentiation
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify why dy/dx must be attached via the chain rule every time y is differentiated
Ask them to solve for dy/dx as a distinct algebraic step at the end
common_errors: Forgetting to multiply by dy/dx when differentiating a term containing y
Treating x and y asymmetrically when both should get chain rule treatment

topics.name: Related Rates
prompt_hints: Require the student to write the relevant equation relating the variables BEFORE differentiating with respect to time
Ask them to justify which rates are given and which is unknown before solving
common_errors: Substituting known numeric values before differentiating instead of after
Misidentifying which quantity's rate of change is actually being asked for

topics.name: Derivatives of Trig, Exponential, and Log Functions
prompt_hints: Ask the student to justify the derivative of e^x as the unique function that is its own derivative
Push them to be careful with chain rule when trig/exp/log functions have non-x arguments
common_errors: Confusing the derivatives of sin and cos (sign error)
Forgetting the chain rule factor when the argument of ln, e, or a trig function isn't simply x

topics.name: MVT and Rolle's Theorem
prompt_hints: Require the student to verify the hypotheses (continuity, differentiability) before applying MVT or Rolle's theorem
Ask them to justify what the theorem guarantees versus what it doesn't
common_errors: Applying MVT without checking differentiability on the open interval
Assuming MVT identifies where the guaranteed point is, not just that it exists

topics.name: Increasing/Decreasing and the First Derivative Test
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify sign changes in the first derivative using a sign chart, not guessing
Ask them to connect increasing/decreasing behavior directly to the sign of f'(x), not f(x)
common_errors: Using the sign of f(x) instead of f'(x) to determine increasing/decreasing
Missing critical points where f' is undefined, not just where f'=0

topics.name: Concavity and the Second Derivative Test
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify inflection points as places where concavity actually changes, not just where f''=0
Ask them to distinguish clearly between the first derivative test and second derivative test
common_errors: Calling every point where f''=0 an inflection point without checking that concavity actually changes there
Confusing concavity with increasing/decreasing behavior

topics.name: Optimization
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify their constraint equation before substituting into the objective function
Ask them to verify a critical point is actually a max or min using the first or second derivative test
common_errors: Finding a critical point and assuming it's the answer without verifying it's a maximum or minimum
Forgetting to check endpoints on a closed interval

topics.name: Curve Sketching
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify each feature (intercepts, asymptotes, extrema, inflection points) with actual calculus, not guessing from a rough shape
Ask them to reconcile the first and second derivative information into one consistent sketch
common_errors: Sketching a curve based on a few points without using derivative information to justify shape
Contradicting their own first/second derivative sign chart in the final sketch

topics.name: L'Hopital's Rule
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify that the limit is actually an indeterminate form before applying L'Hopital's rule
Ask them to differentiate numerator and denominator separately, not use the quotient rule
common_errors: Applying L'Hopital's rule to a limit that isn't actually an indeterminate form
Using the quotient rule instead of differentiating numerator and denominator separately

topics.name: Riemann Sums and the Definite Integral
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify how a Riemann sum approximates area, and how the definite integral is its limit
Ask them to distinguish left, right, and midpoint sums and when each over- or under-estimates
common_errors: Assuming all Riemann sum types give the same approximation
Confusing the definite integral's value with a Riemann sum approximation of it

topics.name: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Parts 1 and 2
prompt_hints: Require the student to state which part of the Fundamental Theorem they're using and justify why it applies
Ask them to be careful with chain rule when the upper limit of integration isn't simply x
common_errors: Confusing FTC Part 1 (differentiating an integral) with Part 2 (evaluating a definite integral)
Forgetting the chain rule factor when the integral's bound is a function of x, not x itself

topics.name: Basic Antiderivatives
prompt_hints: Ask the student to justify their antiderivative by differentiating it back
Push them to remember the +C for indefinite integrals and justify why it's needed
common_errors: Forgetting the constant of integration on indefinite integrals
Misapplying the power rule for integration when the exponent is -1

topics.name: U-Substitution
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify their choice of u and show du explicitly before substituting
Ask them to convert the limits of integration when using u-substitution on a definite integral
common_errors: Substituting u without changing du or accounting for it in the integral
Forgetting to change the limits of integration (or convert back to x) for definite integrals

topics.name: Initial Value Problems
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify using the given initial condition to solve for the constant of integration
Ask them to check their final answer satisfies both the differential equation and the initial condition
common_errors: Forgetting to apply the initial condition to solve for C
Solving for C using the wrong point

topics.name: Area Between Curves
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify which function is on top (or right) before setting up the integral
Ask them to identify intersection points as the bounds of integration, with reasoning, not just by inspection
common_errors: Subtracting functions in the wrong order, producing a negative area
Using incorrect bounds by not solving for actual intersection points

topics.name: Accumulation Functions
prompt_hints: Push the student to interpret an accumulation function as net change, justified by FTC
Ask them to distinguish net change from total accumulated amount when the rate changes sign
common_errors: Confusing net change with total accumulated amount when the integrand changes sign
Misreading an accumulation function graph's meaning at a given point

topics.name: Average Value of a Function
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify the average value formula as (1/(b-a)) times the definite integral
Ask them to connect this back to the Mean Value Theorem for integrals conceptually
common_errors: Forgetting to divide by (b-a) after computing the definite integral
Confusing average value of a function with average rate of change

topics.name: Particle Motion with Integrals
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify the difference between total distance and displacement using absolute value of velocity
Ask them to identify when the particle changes direction before computing distance
common_errors: Computing displacement when the question asks for total distance traveled, or vice versa
Forgetting to split the integral at points where velocity changes sign when finding total distance

topics.name: Slope Fields
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify the slope drawn at each point using the differential equation itself
Ask them to sketch a solution curve consistent with the slope field and a given initial condition
common_errors: Drawing slopes that don't match the differential equation at that point
Sketching a solution curve that crosses slope lines inconsistently

topics.name: Separation of Variables
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify why variables can be separated before integrating both sides
Ask them to apply the initial condition after integrating, not before
common_errors: Forgetting to include the constant of integration when separating variables
Losing track of which variable belongs on which side during separation

topics.name: Exponential Growth and Decay Models
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify why dy/dt = ky leads to exponential behavior, not just memorize the formula
Ask them to interpret k's sign in context (growth vs decay)
common_errors: Confusing the sign of k between growth and decay scenarios
Misapplying the exponential model to a situation that isn't actually proportional growth

topics.name: Integration by Parts
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify their choice of u and dv (e.g., using LIATE) before proceeding
Ask them to check whether repeated integration by parts is needed and why
common_errors: Choosing u and dv in a way that makes the resulting integral more complex, not less
Forgetting the sign in the integration by parts formula

topics.name: Partial Fractions
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify the decomposition setup based on the denominator's factors before solving for constants
Ask them to check their decomposition by recombining it back into a single fraction
common_errors: Setting up an incorrect partial fraction form for repeated or irreducible quadratic factors
Making algebra errors when solving for the unknown constants

topics.name: Improper Integrals
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify rewriting the improper integral as a limit before evaluating
Ask them to determine convergence or divergence explicitly, not just compute a number
common_errors: Evaluating an improper integral as if it were a normal definite integral, without the limit
Concluding convergence without actually checking the limit exists and is finite

topics.name: Parametric Derivatives
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify dy/dx as (dy/dt)/(dx/dt), not a single differentiation step
Ask them to be careful applying the quotient rule again for the second derivative
common_errors: Differentiating y with respect to x directly instead of using the parametric derivative formula
Using the wrong formula for the second derivative of a parametric curve

topics.name: Arc Length (Parametric)
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify the arc length formula as coming from the Pythagorean theorem applied to (dx)^2 + (dy)^2
Ask them to set up the integral with correct bounds in terms of t
common_errors: Using the arc length formula in terms of x instead of the parametric (t-based) version
Forgetting to take the square root before integrating

topics.name: Speed and Distance (Parametric)
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify speed as the magnitude of the velocity vector, sqrt((dx/dt)^2 + (dy/dt)^2)
Ask them to distinguish speed from the individual velocity components
common_errors: Reporting a velocity component as if it were the speed
Forgetting to take the square root when computing speed from velocity components

topics.name: Vector-Valued Functions
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify that differentiating a vector-valued function means differentiating each component separately
Ask them to interpret the derivative as a velocity vector, tangent to the path
common_errors: Treating a vector-valued function as a single scalar function when differentiating or integrating
Misinterpreting the derivative vector's direction relative to the path

topics.name: Polar Curves and Graphing
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify key points on a polar graph by evaluating r at specific angles, not guessing the shape
Ask them to explain what a negative r value means when plotting
common_errors: Assuming polar graphs always pass through the origin the same way a Cartesian graph would
Mishandling negative r values when plotting points

topics.name: Derivatives in Polar
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify converting to x = r cos(theta), y = r sin(theta) before finding dy/dx
Ask them to apply the parametric derivative approach since polar curves are parametrized by theta
common_errors: Trying to differentiate r with respect to theta and calling it dy/dx directly
Forgetting the product rule when differentiating x and y in terms of theta

topics.name: Area in Polar Coordinates
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify the polar area formula as built from infinitesimal circular sectors, not rectangles
Ask them to identify correct bounds of theta, especially when curves overlap
common_errors: Using the Cartesian area formula instead of the polar sector formula
Using incorrect theta bounds when regions are bounded by two different curves

topics.name: Sequences and Convergence
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify convergence by evaluating the limit of the sequence's general term as n approaches infinity
Ask them to distinguish a sequence from a series explicitly
common_errors: Confusing a sequence with the series formed by summing it
Concluding convergence without properly evaluating the limit of the general term

topics.name: Geometric Series
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify the convergence condition |r| < 1 before using the sum formula
Ask them to identify the first term and common ratio explicitly before applying the formula
common_errors: Applying the geometric series sum formula when |r| >= 1
Misidentifying the first term, especially when the series doesn't start at n=0

topics.name: Integral Test
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify that the function is positive, continuous, and decreasing before applying the integral test
Ask them to connect the convergence of the improper integral directly to the convergence of the series
common_errors: Applying the integral test without checking the function is decreasing
Concluding the series' sum equals the integral's value instead of just matching convergence behavior

topics.name: Comparison Tests
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify the inequality between the given series and the comparison series explicitly, term by term
Ask them to pick a comparison series whose convergence behavior is already known
common_errors: Comparing to a series without verifying the inequality holds for all relevant n
Using the comparison test in the wrong direction

topics.name: Ratio and Root Tests
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify computing the limit correctly and interpreting the result relative to 1
Ask them to note that these tests are inconclusive when the limit equals exactly 1
common_errors: Concluding convergence or divergence when the ratio/root test limit equals 1 (it's inconclusive)
Algebra errors when simplifying the ratio of consecutive terms

topics.name: Alternating Series and Error Bound
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify the alternating series test's two conditions (decreasing terms, limit to zero) before applying it
Ask them to use the error bound as the magnitude of the first omitted term, and justify why
common_errors: Applying the alternating series error bound to a series that isn't actually alternating or decreasing
Using the wrong term (not the first omitted one) as the error bound

topics.name: Power Series and Radius of Convergence
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify using the ratio test to find the radius of convergence before checking endpoints separately
Ask them to explicitly test both endpoints, since the ratio test doesn't determine convergence there
common_errors: Forgetting to check the endpoints of the interval of convergence separately
Concluding the interval of convergence without justifying endpoint behavior with a different test

topics.name: Taylor and Maclaurin Series
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify each coefficient using the Taylor series formula involving derivatives at the center point
Ask them to distinguish a Maclaurin series as simply a Taylor series centered at zero
common_errors: Computing Taylor coefficients with an error in the factorial or derivative order
Confusing the center of the Taylor series with x=0 when a different center is specified

topics.name: Taylor Polynomial Error (Lagrange Remainder)
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify the Lagrange remainder bound using the correct order derivative and interval
Ask them to explain what the remainder represents: the error between the polynomial approximation and the actual function
common_errors: Using the wrong order of derivative in the Lagrange remainder formula
Failing to bound the derivative over the correct interval when estimating the maximum error

topics.name: Euler's Method
prompt_hints: Push the student to justify each step as a linear approximation using the slope at the current point
Ask them to explain how step size affects the accuracy of Euler's method's approximation
common_errors: Using the slope at the wrong point for a given step
Assuming Euler's method gives an exact solution rather than an approximation

topics.name: Logistic Growth Model
prompt_hints: Require the student to justify the logistic model's carrying capacity as the value where growth rate goes to zero
Ask them to explain why growth rate is fastest at half the carrying capacity
common_errors: Confusing the logistic growth model with simple exponential growth, ignoring the carrying capacity term
Assuming growth rate is constant rather than changing as the population approaches carrying capacity

common_misconceptions.description: Students give a correct final answer without showing supporting work or notation — this scores zero on the actual AP Calculus exam even with a correct number.
detection_hints: Check whether intermediate steps and proper notation are shown, not just a final boxed answer

common_misconceptions.description: Students apply a convergence test without verifying its required conditions hold, or misinterpret an inconclusive result as proof of convergence or divergence.
detection_hints: Check whether the student explicitly verifies the test's conditions before applying it
Watch for treating a ratio/root test result of exactly 1 as conclusive

common_misconceptions.description: Students confuse the convergence of a sequence (its terms approaching a limit) with the convergence of the series formed by summing that sequence.
detection_hints: Check whether the student is discussing the limit of terms or the sum, and whether they're using the right one for the question asked

common_misconceptions.description: Students drop the +C on indefinite integrals, or forget to solve for it using an initial condition when one is given.
detection_hints: Check indefinite integral answers for a missing +C
Check whether an initial condition given in the problem was actually used

common_misconceptions.description: Students forget to apply the chain rule's inner-function derivative factor, especially in implicit differentiation and derivatives of composite trig/exp/log functions.
detection_hints: Check whether a derivative of a composite function is missing an inner-derivative factor

common_misconceptions.description: Students find a radius of convergence using the ratio test but never separately check the endpoints of the interval, which the ratio test cannot determine.
detection_hints: Check whether both endpoints of the interval are tested individually with a different convergence test

common_misconceptions.description: Students confuse net change (a definite integral) with total accumulated distance or amount when the integrand changes sign.
detection_hints: Check whether the student split the integral at sign changes when total distance/amount, not net change, was asked for

common_misconceptions.description: Students apply the alternating series error bound without first verifying the series terms are decreasing and approach zero.
detection_hints: Check whether the two alternating series test conditions were verified before using the error bound

frq_rubric.general_guidance: Calculus FRQs require showing all work — a correct answer with no supporting work scores zero. Key requirements: proper notation (especially for integrals and derivatives), correct use of theorems by name where applicable (FTC, MVT), and units on any applied problem. For BC series questions: always state the convergence test being used and verify all conditions of the test are met before applying it.
frq_rubric.point_allocation_pattern: AP Calculus FRQs typically award points for each of: setting up the correct expression or equation, correct use of a named theorem or rule where relevant (FTC, MVT, a specific convergence test), correct execution of calculus mechanics (differentiation, integration, algebra), and a final answer with correct units or interpretation in context. Work shown that supports each step earns credit even if a later step contains an error.
common_reasoning_gaps: Gives a correct final answer without any supporting work or proper notation
Applies a convergence test without verifying its required conditions hold
Uses a theorem (FTC, MVT) without naming it or justifying why it applies
Confuses net change with total accumulated distance or amount
Omits units or context interpretation on applied problems
